item.title: Iraq's top court says Baghdad can deploy troops to secure borders in Kurdistan region
item.description:
By Muayad Hameed and Tala Ramadan

BAGHDAD, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Iraq's highest court ruled on Wednesday that Baghdad can deploy federal forces along all international borders, including in the semi-autonomous Kurdistan region,backing Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's push to assert more central control.

Zaidi ordered federal authorities on Tuesday to take over border crossings run by the Kurdistan Regional Government, and has also demanded authority over oil fields controlled by Kurdish security forces, following a probe into smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company.

item.title: In Lebanon, the opening of a second airport reflects political shifts
item.description:
By Laila Bassam and Nazih Osseiran

KLEIAT AIRPORT, Lebanon, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Lebanon plans to open a second international airport next month to bring economic growth to the poorer north, in a project that underlines the diminished political sway of the Hezbollah group, which had long opposed it.

Kleiat Airport, located on the Mediterranean coast, about 20 km (12 miles) from the border crossing to Syria, will offer another gateway to Lebanon alongside Beirut international airport, where travel has been disrupted by wars between Israel and Hezbollah in recent years.

item.title: Pope Leo calls COP31 failure 'troubling,' urges action on climate change
item.description:
By Joshua McElwee

VATICAN CITY, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Pope Leo on Wednesday sharply criticised the failure of UN climate talks over the weekend, calling the outcome "troubling" and urging world leaders to step up efforts to combat climate change.

"In the face of the growing frequency of extreme environmental events linked to the climate crisis, it is troubling that COP 31 ended without the international community adopting clear commitments to address it seriously and responsibly," the pope told pilgrims at his weekly audience in St. Peter's Square.

item.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, his wife and children
item.description:
By Nidal al-Mughrabi

CAIRO, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Israel's military killed a senior Hamas security official as well as his wife and two children with an airstrike on their Gaza Strip apartment early on Wednesday, Gaza's Hamas-run Interior Ministry and medics said.

The airstrike that killed Mohammad Abuelouf, a Hamas colonel who headed the militants' internal security service in northern Gaza, and his family was the second Israeli attack to kill a senior Hamas security official in the past 24 hours.

item.title: Iran says it is prepared to withstand US blockade, seeks to curb price rises
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Iran's first vice president said on Wednesday Tehran was not concerned about a US naval blockade as there had been a significant increase in cargo through other borders, and that the government was seeking to rein in price rises.

Tehran is facing one of its worst inflation surges in decades, driven by the nearly nine-month-old Iran war, with a particularly sharp rise in food prices.

item.title: Jordan sentences man to death over attack that killed officer
item.description:
Nov 25 (Reuters) - Jordan's State Security Court on Wednesday sentenced a man to death over an attack that killed a security officer in the capital Amman earlier this month, the armed forces said in a statement.

The officer was stabbed near the Sri Lankan embassy on November 5, less ​than two weeks after gunmen opened fire at a church in the southern Karak governorate, both rare assaults in the relatively stable US ally.

The court convicted the man of carrying out terrorist acts resulting in death, and of possession of a weapon for terrorist purposes, the statement read.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery
item.description:
Nov 25 (Reuters) - Yemen's Iran-alignedHouthis said on Wednesday they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the kingdom's largest, which is near a major export terminal for Saudi crude.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the refinery attack caused fires.

The Houthi militia, which controls much of western Yemen including the capital Sanaa, has been firing at Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and office buildings since Yemen's frozen civil war reignited in July in a spillover from the US-Iran war.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis threaten to target Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports
item.description: Nov 25 (Reuters) - Yemen's Houthis said on Wednesday the Saudi Arabian port of Jeddah and all other Saudi ports on the Red Sea coast would be targeted if Saudi Arabia carried out threats to attack the Yemeni port of Hodeidah.

item.title: China's Huawei convicted in sprawling US criminal trial over Iran business
item.description:
By Karen Freifeld

NEW YORK, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Chinese telecoms equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran andconspired to steal trade secrets from American companies.

The verdict came in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks.

item.title: Israel's Eisenkot faces new coalition challenge as left-wing faction suspends talks
item.description:
By Steven Scheer

JERUSALEM, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot faced a fresh challenge on Tuesday in his long-shot bid to unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after a left-wing faction suspended coalition talks, further complicating his potential path to power.

The left-wing Democrats' announcement that they were halting talks with Eisenkot came even as his Yashar party said it had reached a coalition deal with a right-wing faction whose support is viewed as critical to him potentially forming a government.

item.title: Senior member of Turkish ruling party resigns amid fund probe
item.description:
ANKARA, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Hayati Yazici, a senior member and founder of Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party, said on Tuesday he was resigning from the party's leadership as a probe into alleged market manipulation and insider trading widened to include his son.

Since September, Turkish investment funds that had concentrated their holdings in thinly traded stocks have been unable to meet investor withdrawals, prompting regulators to liquidate 131 funds and launch a criminal probe that has involved several senior officials and members of government.

item.title: Israel's defense minister accuses Iran of developing chemical weapons: What to know
item.description: Israel says Iran is pursuing chemical weapons and signals readiness for joint military action, but a US source questions the allegations as opposition mounts to Netanyahu’s push for strikes.

item.title: Houthis won't seize Aden, Yemeni government forces say
item.description:
By Phil Stewart and Timour Azhari

WASHINGTON/RIYADH, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have pushed as close as 60 km (37 miles) to Aden, the temporary capital of the country's internationally recognised government, but they will not capture the city, Yemen's military said on Tuesday.

"I'll speak to you frankly. The situation is not where we want it to be. But it's not as dire as reported," Colonel Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaily, spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, told a group of reporters via video link.

item.title: Turkish military helicopter crashes during training flight, killing 5
item.description: The crash marks the second in less than two weeks after another helicopter went down on Nov. 12, killing all four onboard.

item.title: Iraqi Kurds close ranks as Baghdad moves to seize oil, border control
item.description: The KDP and the PUK set aside their bitter rivalries to oppose Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s push to bring the Kurdistan Region’s oil fields and border crossings under Baghdad’s control.
